item_inventory.claim_and_conventions:
Let $M\subset\mathbb R^{d_a}$ be a compact smooth manifold of dimension $n\ge d$, let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a bounded domain, and let $\sigma\in C^\infty(\mathbb R)$ be globally Lipschitz and nonpolynomial. Fix finite input and output channel dimensions. A generalized Fourier neural operator is a map $\Psi:L^2(M;\mathbb R^{d_{in}})\to L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^{d_{out}})$ of the form
$$\Psi=Q\circ R\circ F\circ L_L\circ\cdots\circ L_1\circ E\circ S.$$
Here $S$ is a pointwise finite-dimensional affine network, $S(h)(x)=s(x,h(x))$; $E$ is a continuous linear chart-lifting map from manifold functions to multichannel functions on $\mathbb T^n$; each $L_\ell$ acts on periodic channel fields by a fixed matrix channel map plus a continuous periodic channel bias $b_\ell(x)$ and a finite Fourier-multiplier convolution, followed coordinatewise by $\sigma$; $F:L^2(\mathbb T^n;\mathbb R^{c})\to L^2(\mathbb T^d;\mathbb R^{r})$ is a continuous linear dimension-reduction layer
$$ (Fv)(x_1,\ldots,x_d)=\int_{\mathbb T^{n-d}}K(z)v(x_1,\ldots,x_d,z)\,dz,$$
with a finite-dimensional matrix kernel $K$; $R$ is restriction of periodic fields to $\Omega$; and $Q$ is a pointwise finite-dimensional output network. For the EIT boundary manifold $M=\partial\Omega\times\partial\Omega$, the chart-lifting map $E$ may be taken to be the map $G$ of the chart-lifting lemma, with its finite chart-pair array treated as input channels. The finite Fourier multiplier at a layer is $\widehat{\mathcal K v}(k)=R_k\widehat v(k)$ for finitely many $k\in\mathbb Z^n$, with real-valued outputs enforced by conjugate-symmetric coefficients. When $n=d$, $F$ is the identity layer.

This is an architecture definition only. It asserts no approximation, training, statistical, discretization, or computational-cost guarantee.

item_inventory.claim_and_conventions:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be nonempty, bounded, connected and $C^1$, and let $\gamma\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $0<m\le\gamma\le M<\infty$ almost everywhere. Let $\mathcal D(\Omega)=H^1(\Omega)/H_0^1(\Omega)$ be the trace quotient and write $\dot{\mathcal D}=\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb R\mathbf1$. For each $F\in\dot{\mathcal D}^{*}$ there is a unique weak solution class $[u]\in H^1(\Omega)/\mathbb R\mathbf1$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\nabla u\cdot\overline{\nabla v}\,dx=F([\operatorname{Tr}v])\qquad(v\in H^1(\Omega)).$$
The resulting solution operator $\mathscr R_\gamma:\dot{\mathcal D}^{*}\to\dot{\mathcal D}$ is bounded. Its unique representative whose boundary trace has surface mean zero solves the same weak equation. In particular, for $f\in L^2(\partial\Omega)$ with $\int_{\partial\Omega}f\,dS=0$, the functional $F_f([g])=\int_{\partial\Omega}f\overline g\,dS$ is admissible and defines the mean-zero Neumann-to-Dirichlet map on mean-zero $L^2$ fluxes.

item_inventory.claim_and_conventions:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be nonempty, bounded, connected and $C^\infty$, and let $\gamma\in X_d(R)$ be a real conductivity. Write $M=\partial\Omega$, let $dS$ be surface measure, and set
$$L^2_0(M)=\left\{f\in L^2(M):\int_M f\,dS=0\right\},\qquad P_0f=f-|M|^{-1}\int_Mf\,dS.$$
The mean-zero Neumann-to-Dirichlet operator $\mathscr R_\gamma:L^2_0(M)\to L^2_0(M)$ sends $f$ to the mean-zero boundary trace of the weak solution of $\nabla\cdot(\gamma\nabla u)=0$ with outward conormal flux $f$, as defined by the weak Neumann problem. Let $-\Delta_M$ be the nonnegative Laplace–Beltrami operator on the compact boundary manifold, with eigenpairs $(e_j,\lambda_j)$ on $L^2_0(M)$ from its spectral resolution. For $\tau=1/2$ when $d=2$ and any fixed $\tau>0$ when $d\ge3$, put
$$r_d:=\frac{d-1}{2}-1+\tau,\qquad C_M^{r_d/2}e_j=(1+\lambda_j)^{-r_d/2}e_j.$$
The smoothed observation is the bounded operator $A_\gamma:=\mathscr R_\gamma C_M^{r_d/2}:L^2_0(M)\to L^2_0(M)$. Its extension to all of $L^2(M)$ is $\widetilde A_\gamma f=\iota_0A_\gamma(P_0f)$, where $\iota_0:L^2_0(M)\hookrightarrow L^2(M)$ is inclusion. Thus its integral kernel, when it exists in $L^2(M\times M)$, is fixed to have zero mean in each variable. No assertion of a kernel's existence or Hilbert–Schmidt regularity is part of this definition.

item_inventory.claim_and_conventions:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded connected smooth domain, let $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$, let $0<m\le1\le M<\infty$, and let $m\le\gamma\le M$ be measurable with $\gamma=1$ outside $\Omega'$. Put $M_\partial=\partial\Omega$ and give the NtD maps their total-boundary-mean-zero representatives. The spectral space $H^{1/2}_\Delta(M_\partial)$ is equivalent to the chart trace space $H^{1/2}(M_\partial)$, including their quotients by constants and mean-zero duals. Uniformly in $\gamma$,
$$\|\mathscr R_\gamma f\|_{H^1_\Delta(M_\partial)}\le C\|f\|_{L^2(M_\partial)}\quad\left(\int_{M_\partial}f=0\right).$$
For every integer $q\ge0$ there is $C_q$ such that
$$\|(\mathscr R_\gamma-\mathscr R_1)F\|_{H^q_\Delta(M_\partial)}\le C_q\|F\|_{H^{-1/2}_\Delta(M_\partial)}$$
for every mean-zero weak Neumann flux $F$. If $w_j=1+\lambda_j$ and $(e_j)$ is any orthonormal boundary Laplace–Beltrami basis on the total-mean-zero subspace, the matrix $b_{ij}=\langle(\mathscr R_\gamma-\mathscr R_{\gamma_0})e_j,e_i\rangle$ of any two such conductivities satisfies, for every $L>0$,
$$|b_{ij}|\le C_L(w_iw_j)^{-L}.$$
The constants depend only on the displayed fixed data and $q$ or $L$. More generally, any $v\in H^1$ harmonic with zero weak normal derivative on a fixed smooth boundary collar has $\|v|_{M_\partial}\|_{H^q_\Delta}\le C_q\|v\|_{H^1(\text{collar})}$ for every integer $q\ge0$, using a fixed smaller collar for the boundary estimate.

$$\| (\mathscr R_\gamma-\mathscr R_{\gamma_0})(1-\Delta_{\partial\Omega})^{-r/2}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\le C_r\|\gamma-\gamma_0\|_{L^q(\Omega)}.$$
It also satisfies the same bound with the coefficient $L^\infty$ norm in place of $L^q$. Constants depend only on the displayed fixed geometry, ellipticity and exponents.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H_1,H_2$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $A\subseteq H_1$, and let $g:A\to H_2$. If a continuous, nondecreasing, concave function $\omega_\star:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ satisfies $\omega_\star(0)=0$ and
$$\|g(x)-g(y)\|_{H_2}\le\omega_\star(\|x-y\|_{H_1})\qquad(x,y\in A),$$
then the Hilbert-valued same-modulus extension theorem asserts that there is $\widetilde g:H_1\to H_2$ extending $g$ and satisfying the same inequality for every $x,y\in H_1$.

For the EIT inverse map, if IP-45 gives $\|\gamma-\gamma_0\|_2\le C_0[\log(1/\min\{\delta,t_0\})]^{-\rho}$ for $\delta=\|\dot\Lambda_\gamma-\dot\Lambda_{\gamma_0}\|$, and the NTD kernel estimate transfers $\delta\le C_1\|\kappa_\gamma-\kappa_{\gamma_0}\|_2^{1/2}$, then after decreasing $t_0$ and, if necessary, enlarging $C_0$ the concave modulus
$$\omega_\star(0)=0,\qquad \omega_\star(s)=C_0\left[\log\!\left(\frac1{\min\{C_1\sqrt{s},t_0\}}\right)\right]^{-\rho}\quad(s>0)$$
is an admissible modulus for that inverse map and can be extended by the Hilbert same-modulus theorem.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be nonempty, bounded, connected and $C^\infty$, let $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$, and fix the ellipticity, collar and regularity parameters defining $X_d(R)$. Let $M=\partial\Omega$, let $K\subset L^2(M\times M)$ be compact, and for $\delta\ge0$ put $K_\delta=\{\eta\in K:\|\eta\|_{L^2(M\times M)}\le\delta\}$. Let $\kappa_\gamma$ be the zero-mean-in-each-variable kernel of the dimension-dependently smoothed mean-zero NtD observation for $\gamma\in X_d(R)$. Let $\widetilde\Psi^\star:L^2(M\times M)\to L^2(\Omega)$ extend the exact-data inverse map and satisfy
$$\|\widetilde\Psi^\star(f)-\widetilde\Psi^\star(g)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C_\star\omega_\star(\|f-g\|_{L^2(M\times M)}),$$
where $\omega_\star$ is continuous, nondecreasing and concave with $\omega_\star(0)=0$. Then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a generalized Fourier neural operator $\Psi:L^2(M\times M)\to L^2(\Omega)$ such that
$$\sup_{\gamma\in X_d(R),\,\eta\in K_\delta}\|\gamma-\Psi(\kappa_\gamma+\eta)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le\varepsilon+C_\star\omega_\star(\delta).$$
This is an existence statement for continuum NtD kernels and compact noise sets; it makes no training, finite-sample, network-size, finite-element, electrode-matrix or calibration guarantee.

item_inventory.claim_and_conventions:
Fix the continuum EIT data set $\mathcal Z=\{(\kappa_\gamma+\eta,\gamma):\gamma\in X_d(R),\ \eta\in K_\delta\}$ in $\mathcal H\times\mathcal Y$, where $\mathcal H=L^2(\partial\Omega\times\partial\Omega)$ is the input space and $\mathcal Y=L^2(\Omega)$ is the target space. Assume $\mathcal Z$ is nonempty and compact, and set $X=\{x\in\mathcal H:(x,y)\in\mathcal Z\text{ for some }y\in\mathcal Y\}$. Fix a smooth globally Lipschitz nonpolynomial activation and the generalized-FNO architecture on the boundary manifold. For integers $s\ge1$ and $B>0$, let $\mathcal F_{s,B}\subset C(X,\mathcal Y)$ be the restrictions to $X$ of generalized FNOs with depth, channel width, Fourier cutoff and number of trainable scalar parameters at most $s$, every trainable scalar coefficient bounded in absolute value by $B$, and coordinate bias functions restricted to Fourier modes of cutoff at most $s$, where $C(X,\mathcal Y)$ denotes continuous maps with the supremum norm. Consider only $s,B$ for which $\mathcal F_{s,B}$ is nonempty and $\sup_{\Psi\in\mathcal F_{s,B},\,x\in X}\|\Psi(x)\|_{\mathcal Y}<\infty$. Give $\mathcal F_{s,B}$ the Borel sigma-algebra induced by this norm. For $z=(x,y)\in\mathcal Z$ and $\Psi\in\mathcal F_{s,B}$, define $\ell(z,\Psi)=\|\Psi(x)-y\|_{\mathcal Y}^2$. For a Borel probability law $P$ on $\mathcal Z$, put $R_P(\Psi)=\mathbb E_{Z\sim P}\ell(Z,\Psi)$ and $\widehat R_N(\Psi)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\ell(Z_i,\Psi)$ for iid $Z_i\sim P$. Determine the minimax excess-risk behavior
$$\mathfrak R_N(s,B):=\inf_{\widehat\Psi_N}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Z)}\mathbb E_{P^N}\left[R_P(\widehat\Psi_N)-\inf_{\Psi\in\mathcal F_{s,B}}R_P(\Psi)\right],$$
where $\mathcal P(\mathcal Z)$ is the set of Borel probability laws on $\mathcal Z$ and the infimum is over Borel learners $\widehat\Psi_N:\mathcal Z^N\to\mathcal F_{s,B}$. Characterize growth regimes $s=s_N$, $B=B_N$ in which estimation and continuum approximation errors can be balanced while retaining the deterministic noise term $C_\star\omega_\star(\delta)$.
